meta.scope: Peru batch 2 — Short-term activity & manufacturing, external sector (BOP, trade), and deeper BCR policy layer (inflation report, reference rate, reserves).

candidates.title: Producción Nacional / Monthly GDP (PBI)
candidates.description: Monthly estimate of national production (PBI) by economic activity. Principal high-frequency real-activity indicator.
candidates.notes: Core short-term activity product. 2025 full-year growth ~3.4%; Q1 2026 ~3.5%. Construction, commerce and manufacturing have been recent drivers.

candidates.title: PBI Manufactura / Manufacturing production
candidates.description: Volume and value indicators of manufacturing production, split into primary and non-primary manufacturing. Monthly and annual series.
candidates.notes: Manufacturing contributes ~12% of GDP. 2025 growth ~2.7% (primary +4.9%, non-primary +1.9%). Export-oriented manufacturing has been a notable contributor.

candidates.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
candidates.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
candidates.notes: Core external-accounts product. Recent years have shown current-account surpluses driven by strong traditional exports (mining, fishing, gas). Net international investment position and reserve adequacy are regularly reported.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
candidates.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, classified as traditional (mining, fishing, agriculture, oil/gas) and non-traditional.
candidates.notes: Trade data feed both the BOP and the national accounts. Mining remains the dominant traditional export; manufacturing exports have shown strong recent growth.

candidates.title: Reporte de Inflación (BCR)
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
candidates.description: Periodic Inflation Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the reference interest rate under the explicit inflation-targeting regime.
candidates.notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements the monthly monetary-programme statements. Central reference for the 1–3% inflation target band.

candidates.title: Tasa de interés de referencia / Policy interest rate
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
candidates.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCR Board. The rate at which the central bank signals the monetary stance and steers interbank rates.
candidates.notes: Operational policy rate. Held at 4.25% for an extended period in 2025–2026 after the earlier easing cycle. Path is the primary signal of the monetary stance.

candidates.title: Reservas Internacionales Netas (RIN)
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
candidates.description: Stock of net international reserves managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and annual reports.
candidates.notes: Key external-buffer indicator. End-2025 RIN ~USD 90 bn (~26% of GDP), covering multiple months of imports and a high multiple of short-term external debt.

candidates.title: Marco de metas de inflación (1–3%) — BCR
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
candidates.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting with a 1–3% annual CPI band (centre 2%). In place since 2002.
referenced_by: Every Inflation Report and monetary-programme statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Peruvian monetary policy
candidates.notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.

candidates.title: Producción y exportaciones mineras / Mining production & exports
candidates.publisher: INEI / Ministerio de Energía y Minas / BCR
candidates.description: Statistics of metallic and non-metallic mining production and exports (copper, gold, zinc, silver, etc.). Structural component of traditional exports and of GDP.
candidates.notes: Mining is the backbone of traditional exports and a major GDP contributor. Copper and gold dominate the export basket; production and export volumes are high-frequency inputs into the BOP and national accounts.

candidates.title: Producción y exportaciones pesqueras / Fishing & fishmeal
candidates.description: Statistics of fishing catch, fishmeal and fish-oil production and exports. Important traditional export and source of short-term volatility in manufacturing and GDP.
candidates.notes: High-volatility traditional sector. Anchovy/fishmeal cycles drive large swings in primary manufacturing and in the goods trade balance. Regularly highlighted in monthly production and BOP analysis.

proposed_edges.basis: Manufacturing is a major component of the monthly national-production estimate.
Balance of payments is compiled by the Banco Central de Reserva.
Merchandise trade flows are a primary input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
The Inflation Report analyses outcomes against the 1–3% target band.
The reference rate is the primary instrument used to steer inflation toward the target.
Changes in reserve assets appear in the balance of payments.
Mining products are the dominant traditional export line.
Fishmeal and related processing form a large part of primary manufacturing.
